title: Molecular basis of tRNA substrate recognition and modification by the atypical SPOUT methyltransferase Trm10.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the Europe PMC supplement (20 MB: 18 figure images plus one 21-page PDF, no spreadsheets at all). Queried the RCSB Protein Data Bank entry records for all three accessions: 9XZQ (3.63 Angstrom, cryo-EM), 9XZR (3.37 A), 9XZS (3.89 A), each with 2 polymer chains (one Trm10 protein, one tRNA). Grepped the full open-access text for every table and quantitative assay reference.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That Table 1 is the cryo-EM data-collection and refinement statistics table for the three structures, and that Supplementary Table S1 is a residue-conservation listing across Trm10 orthologs (both read in the text, not opened as files). The binding constants (apparent dissociation constant, n = 3 replicates) and radiolabel methyltransferase activity assays cover only four proteins: wild-type Trm10 plus the Trm10-delta-47, Trm10-delta-63 and Trm10-8A variants, against a single tRNA (glycine-GCC).

a1_downloadable.note: Open: all three Protein Data Bank entries and their Electron Microscopy Data Bank maps resolve and are freely downloadable; I confirmed the entry metadata for 9XZQ, 9XZR and 9XZS directly from RCSB.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no prediction target anywhere in the deposited data. The only conceivable label (is a given tRNA a Trm10 substrate, or how fast is it methylated) exists in no column here; it would have to be assembled from MODOMICS and earlier kinetics papers. Stopped here per the checklist.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not the failing item: protein and RNA sequences and coordinates are present inside the three structure files, so inputs exist even though a target does not.

a4_units_stated.note: Not the failing item: cryo-EM resolutions are in Angstroms and binding constants are reported as apparent dissociation constants with units in the text.

a5_enough_rows.note: Three structures. The supporting biochemistry covers four enzyme variants against one tRNA. Against the threshold of ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification) this is three orders of magnitude short; it is a mechanistic structure paper, not a dataset.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <1 GB (three coordinate files plus three cryo-EM maps)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Not the failing item: trivially small.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not the failing item: the three accessions named in the data availability statement match the three entries I retrieved from RCSB, including the closed/open/dimeric labels.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed in depth because no label exists. Noted for the record: the dimeric-complex interpretation leans on molecular dynamics simulations, which would be model output rather than measurement if used as a target.

existing_models.name: EvoRMD (RNA modification predictor built on an RNA language model, Genome Biology 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as strong across 11 RNA modification types with biological context metadata; I saw only the abstract and summary via search, not the paper's numbers or splits.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Abstract states that most prior methods model each modification type independently; context-conditioned prediction is their stated contribution.

existing_models.name: tRNAmodpred (homology-and-pathway method that maps MODOMICS modification pathways onto input tRNA sequences)
existing_models.score_and_split: Rule/homology based rather than a trained statistical model; no held-out performance number retrieved.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or a similar RNA language model would be the natural backbone for a tRNA-substrate task
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop would suffice for a few hundred tRNA sequences
backbone.licence: Not checked; the project died before this mattered.

integration.partner_dataset: MODOMICS (catalogue of RNA modifications and the positions they occur at) plus GtRNAdb (genomic tRNA gene sequences)
integration.join_key: Organism plus tRNA isotype/anticodon, and position number within the tRNA
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which tRNAs carrying a guanosine at position 9 actually get N1-methylated, and does sequence context alone explain the roughly half-and-half split seen in yeast? The question is real, but this paper contributes three structures to it, not data.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the 13 of 26 yeast guanosine-9 tRNAs already known to be Trm10 substrates, which any working model must separate from the non-substrates.
controls.negative_control: Not applicable; no dataset to shuffle.
controls.external_validation: Trm10 homologs in other species (Schizosaccharomyces pombe, human TRMT10A) have published substrate specificities, but those live in other papers.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is available from this paper: with three structures and four enzyme variants measured against a single tRNA, any model would be fitted to data assembled almost entirely from other publications.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a transfer RNA's sequence and shape to predict whether the enzyme Trm10 methylates its ninth building block.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on transfer RNA (tRNA) sequences, one per molecule, labelled as substrate or non-substrate. This paper supplies 3 structures and binding/activity measurements for 4 enzyme versions against 1 tRNA; the roughly 26 relevant yeast tRNAs would have to come from other papers.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no (or a methylation rate) for whether Trm10 modifies position 9. The ground truth comes from radioactive-label methyltransferase assays and mass-spectrometry modification mapping, all published elsewhere, not in this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying tRNA modification and the human disease gene TRMT10A would like a rule for substrate choice, since none has been found in 15 years. But with only tens of tRNAs per organism, this is a biochemistry question, not a machine-learning one.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper adds 3 cryo-electron microscopy structures and 4 enzyme-variant measurements. Existing RNA modification predictors such as EvoRMD train on transcriptome-wide modification catalogues covering 11 modification types; three structures is not more data.

confidence_score.why: The only replicated numbers are apparent dissociation constants with n = 3 for four proteins against one tRNA. That is far too little to calibrate per-prediction confidence for anything.

models_beatable.why: tRNAmodpred is an older homology-and-pathway method with no published held-out benchmark, so it is beatable in principle; EvoRMD is 2026 and reports strong numbers. But we have no data here to beat either with.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: there is no feature/label table in this paper for an existing model to be a baseline against, and structures of one enzyme-substrate pair do not join to any transcriptome-wide modification dataset on a shared key.

ml_idea: The only task this paper suggests is predicting which guanosine-9-containing tRNAs are Trm10 substrates, from sequence plus predicted flexibility, using a frozen RNA language model with a small classification head. That project would need MODOMICS and GtRNAdb as its actual data source; this paper contributes mechanistic structures, which are at best a source of interpretation afterwards, not training data.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: three coordinate files and three cryo-EM maps load in well under 1 GB. Compute was never the constraint here; the number of labelled examples was.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the deposited data. Three structures and one 21-page supplementary PDF with no spreadsheet — that check took one unzip and three API calls and killed it.

verdict_reason: A structural mechanism paper, not a dataset: 3 cryo-EM structures and 4 enzyme variants tested against 1 tRNA. Fails A2 (no prediction target in any file; it would have to be built from MODOMICS and older kinetics papers) and fails A5 by three orders of magnitude. The supplement I opened contains only figure images and a PDF — no tabular data exists to model.
